title: New realm
subtitle: A separate space in your account, with its own computers, keys and settings.

intro.title: What a realm is
intro.apartV: Keys and shares limited to this realm reach only what is in it.
intro.sharedV: A computer can be in several realms. All-realms keys and Global vault entries reach every realm.
intro.freeV: Making a realm costs nothing. You pay for computers as before.

item.notSeen: Not there yet, may still land
item.retryRefused: Latest try refused, earlier may land
item.unread: Not added yet, couldn't read it
items.unknownHelp: Check again only reads each computer; nothing is sent again.
items.changedHelp: A computer whose realms changed since you picked it is not sent to again. Add again keeps its new realms and adds this one.
items.heldSavedHelp: A computer is in the realm, but its other realms are not what an earlier try sent, so that try may still land and set them back. Check again reads them; Stop tracking stops following that try here and on Computers. The change may still go through.
items.heldElsewhereHelp: Another tab's Computers page holds an earlier try for a computer here. Only that page can check or stop tracking it, so look at its realms there.
dismiss.title: Stop tracking the earlier tries?
dismiss.body: Each may still land later and set that computer's realms back to the list it sent. After Stop tracking nothing here or on Computers will warn you. Check its realms on Computers afterwards.
items.goneHelp: A computer marked "Sent, not there now" took the change, then lost this realm again: its realms were changed since. Add again adds it back.
items.heldHelp: An earlier try may still land later. It sends the whole list of realms the computer had then, so it can undo a realm change made since, including this one. If you add it again, check its realms on Computers afterwards.
items.heldMovedHelp: For a computer whose realms changed, an earlier try may still land later and set its realms back to what they were then. If you add it again, check its realms on Computers afterwards.

faq.whatIs.a: A separate space in your account, with its own computers, keys and settings. Pick it from the realm menu at the top: the lists show what is in it, and anything new you make goes into it. Projects also shows a project from another realm when one of its computers is in this one. Keys and shares limited to a realm see only what is in it. Use one per client, project or experiment.
faq.startsWith.q: What is in a new realm?
faq.startsWith.a: Only what you put in it: the computers you pick in step 2, or nothing. It has no projects, keys or vault entries of its own yet. Keys set to All realms work in it at once, and Global vault entries are shared by every realm.
faq.pickMoves.q: Does adding a computer here take it out of its other realms?
faq.pickMoves.a: No. A computer can be in several realms. Each one you pick joins this realm and keeps the realms it already has. To take one out of a realm later, open Computers, choose Realms… on that computer and untick it. A computer stays in at least one realm.
faq.projects.q: Can I make a new computer in an empty realm?
faq.projects.a: Yes, once the realm has a project. A new computer needs a project in the realm you are in, and Get a computer offers "New project in this realm" when there is none. A computer you add from another realm keeps its own project, and that project's people and access rules apply to it in every realm.
faq.keysShares.q: How do keys and shares work with a realm?
faq.keysShares.a: A key works in All realms, in the realms you pick, or, if you make it while one realm is selected, only in that realm. A key limited to realms can't be widened to All realms later. A share gives someone every computer in one realm, including ones added later. It never includes your other realms, your vault or your wallet, but computers they add and AI they turn on are billed to you. Its key stops when the share ends; SSH keys, program addresses, storage shares and Bot links they set up can keep working. To share only some computers, put them in a new realm and share that.
faq.whatElse.q: What else belongs to a realm?
faq.whatElse.a: Its vault entries: the same name in another realm, or in Global, is a different entry. Its Bots: a Bot runs on one computer and, with permission, can use the other computers of its realm. Its checked rules and hooks for agents, and the stop that ends everything running in it. Its Boards: up to 9 per realm.
faq.cost.a: No. A realm isn't something you rent. It is an id that your computers, projects and keys carry. You pay for computers and servers as before, and adding a computer to a second realm doesn't copy it.
faq.nameColour.q: Where are the name and colour kept?
faq.nameColour.a: The name is saved in your account's vault, so every device you sign in on shows it. Change it any time with Rename realms… in the realm menu. The colour is kept on this device only, and other devices show a colour of their own until you pick one there. A name can be up to 64 characters and can't be all, none, every, any or global.
faq.switchRemove.q: How do I switch realms, or remove one I don't need?
faq.switchRemove.a: Pick a realm, or All realms, from the realm menu at the top (Alt+R; on a phone, tap the realm square). An empty realm may not reopen after a reload; pick it again from the menu. There is no Delete realm: a realm is listed while something is in it or it has a name. To remove one, take its computers, projects, servers and keys out of it, then clear its name with Rename realms… in the realm menu.
